subject.title: [Bug]: `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` breaks `openai-codex` auth/keychain paths on macOS and can fail fresh runtime launch with `SecItemCopyMatching failed -50`

question: Should OpenClaw preserve the macOS managed-service `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` default and isolate Codex/OpenAI keychain auth reads, or change the global macOS runtime CA mode?
rationale: Current source shows the CA default protects launchd TLS setup while Codex/OpenAI auth still has keychain-capable paths, so the fix affects both macOS service reliability and auth-provider behavior.

options.title: Scope auth/keychain environments
options.body: Keep the macOS service CA default and add a narrow no-system-CA or bundled-CA boundary only around affected keychain/auth runtime reads after live macOS proof.

options.title: Change the macOS CA default
options.body: Remove or flip the Darwin default globally only with replacement launchd TLS proof and an upgrade note for existing managed services.

options.title: Wait for live reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue open until a maintainer reproduces the exact current-main failure on macOS and confirms which launch path remains affected.

recommendation.title: Scope auth/keychain environments
recommendation.body: Keep the macOS service CA default and add a narrow no-system-CA or bundled-CA boundary only around affected keychain/auth runtime reads after live macOS proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent history spans Codex keychain handling, Node startup TLS centralization, and scoped external CLI credential discovery.
